ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are three carbon atoms labeled C, connected to one another to form a triangular ring; each carbon atom is also connected to two H atoms, indicating that each carbon satisfies its valence bond requirements by bonding to two hydrogens and two carbons. The question stem states that the three carbon atoms are located at the three corners of an equilateral triangle. Reasoning: Each interior angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°, so the C-C-C bond angles within the ring are forced to be close to 60°. However, saturated carbon is usually sp3 hybridized, with an ideal bond angle of about 109.5°. The three-membered ring of cyclopropane makes the carbon-carbon bond angles much smaller than the ideal angle, so the bond angles do not match the bonding angles preferred by the carbon atoms, producing obvious angle strain, thereby making the molecule less stable.
